# A Noble View of Things Counts Against Its Truth

In this real world of sweat and dirt,[^1] when a view of things is 'noble,' that ought to count as a presumption against its truth, and as a philosophic disqualification.[^2] The prince of darkness may be a gentleman, as we are told he is, but whatever the God of earth and heaven is, he can surely be no gentleman.[^3] His menial services are needed in the dust of our human trials, even more than his dignity is needed in the empyrean.[^4]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "In this real world of sweat and dirt"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "when a view of things is 'noble,' that ought to count as a presumption against its truth, and as a philosophic disqualification."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "The prince of darkness may be a gentleman, as we are told he is, but whatever the God of earth and heaven is, he can surely be no gentleman."
